lessons.title: Premiers mots d'auteur
lessons.oneGoal: Students discover what an author does using simple French words

opening.activity: Show pictures of authors writing. Use gestures: point to self 'Je suis...', point to book 'livre', make writing motion 'auteur écrit'.

mainActivity.activity: Look at familiar books and find author names. Students practice saying 'auteur' while pointing to author name. Play 'author actions' - pretend to write, think, read.
mainActivity.flexibility: If students are shy, let them watch first. If excited, let them act out author actions together.

closing.activity: Circle time: Each student says 'auteur' and makes writing gesture. Show tomorrow we'll think of our own ideas.

decisionPoints: If students seem overwhelmed → Use more gestures, fewer words
If students are engaged → Add more author books to explore
If movement needed → Do author actions (writing, thinking, reading)
lessons.troubleshooting: If vocabulary is too hard, just use 'livre' and gestures for writing
lessons.realWorldConnection: Authors write the books we read every day - just like the ones in our classroom
lessons.progression: Foundation lesson - introduces the concept of being an author

lessons.title: Mes idées spéciales
lessons.oneGoal: Students share one idea they could write about

opening.activity: Review: 'Hier, nous avons parlé d'auteur.' Point to head 'idée', make thinking gesture. 'Auteurs ont des idées.'

mainActivity.activity: Show picture prompts (family, pets, toys, food). Students point to what gives them ideas. Use thought bubbles - students hold bubble and share one idea through pictures or words.
mainActivity.flexibility: Let shy students just point. Excited students can share multiple ideas.

closing.activity: Put ideas in 'idea jar' (pictures or words). 'Demain, nous dessinerons nos idées.'

decisionPoints: If students can't think of ideas → Use family photos or favorite toy prompts
If students have many ideas → Let them draw or say multiple quickly
If language barrier → Accept pointing, gestures, or English mixed in
lessons.troubleshooting: If no ideas come, start with 'Qu'est-ce que tu aimes?' and accept any response
lessons.realWorldConnection: Everyone has special ideas worth sharing - just like when we tell family about our day
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by moving from understanding authors to having personal ideas

lessons.title: Dessiner mes histoires
lessons.oneGoal: Students draw pictures to show their story ideas

opening.activity: Review yesterday's ideas from jar. Model: take idea, say 'Je vais dessiner', draw simple picture while talking.

mainActivity.activity: Students choose their idea and draw. Teacher circulates: 'Qu'est-ce que tu dessines?' Encourage details through questions and gestures.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some may finish quickly - let them add details or start second picture. Others may need encouragement to just draw anything.

closing.activity: Gallery walk - students hold pictures and walk around to see others. Simple comments: 'J'aime ton image.'

decisionPoints: If students worry about 'perfect' drawing → Emphasize that ideas matter more than perfect pictures
If students finish early → Let them add background details or colors
If students are stuck → Help them start with simple shapes or stick figures
lessons.troubleshooting: If perfectionism blocks drawing, model 'good enough' drawing yourself
lessons.realWorldConnection: Pictures help us tell stories when words are hard - like when we draw for family
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by using pictures to express ideas before words

lessons.title: Mots simples, grandes histoires
lessons.oneGoal: Students use 2-3 French words to describe their drawings

opening.activity: Look at yesterday's drawings together. Model: show drawing, say 2-3 simple words 'chat, maison, content'.

mainActivity.activity: Students practice saying 2-3 French words about their picture with partner. Teacher provides word cards as supports. Record some students if they want.
mainActivity.flexibility: Accept mix of French/English. Help with pronunciation but don't correct heavily.

closing.activity: Few volunteers share their words with class. Celebrate effort over perfection.

decisionPoints: If students only know English words → Provide French word cards with pictures
If students are confident → Encourage them to try 4-5 words
If pronunciation is difficult → Focus on communication over perfect accent
lessons.troubleshooting: If students are silent, let them point to word cards instead of speaking
lessons.realWorldConnection: We use words to help others understand our pictures - like when we explain our drawings to family
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by adding simple French words to pictures

lessons.title: Écouter les histoires
lessons.oneGoal: Students listen to simple French stories and identify key elements

opening.activity: Review: 'Nous avons créé nos images et mots.' Today: 'Écouter d'autres auteurs.' Put on 'listening ears' (hands cupped to ears).

mainActivity.activity: Read simple French story with lots of pictures and gestures. Stop to ask 'Qui?' (character), 'Où?' (place), 'Quoi?' (action). Students respond with gestures or simple words.
mainActivity.flexibility: If story is too long, just do part. If students are engaged, read second short story.

closing.activity: Students use story element cards to show what they heard. Simple sharing in circle.

decisionPoints: If students can't follow story → Use more gestures and pause more frequently
If students understand well → Ask simple 'Pourquoi?' questions
If attention wavers → Add movement actions for characters
lessons.troubleshooting: If story is too complex, just focus on pictures and ask 'Qu'est-ce que tu vois?'
lessons.realWorldConnection: We learn by listening to stories around us - just like when family tells us stories
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by learning from other authors' work

lessons.title: Personnages amusants
lessons.oneGoal: Students create and name a simple character

opening.activity: Review yesterday's story characters. 'Qui était dans l'histoire?' Show character cards from story.

mainActivity.activity: Students create their own character - draw or use template. Give character a name (French or English OK). Practice introducing character: 'Voici [name]'.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some may want to make animal characters, others people. All choices are good.

closing.activity: Character parade - students introduce their characters to the class. Quick and fun, no pressure.

decisionPoints: If students can't think of names → Provide list of simple French names with pronunciation
If students want complex characters → Keep it simple but validate their ideas
If students copy others → Celebrate similarities and point out unique details
lessons.troubleshooting: If students are stuck on names, let them use their own name or favorite toy's name
lessons.realWorldConnection: Stories need characters just like our lives have people - family, friends, pets
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by creating their own story elements

lessons.title: Où se passe l'histoire?
lessons.oneGoal: Students choose and describe a simple setting

opening.activity: Bring back characters from yesterday. 'Où habite ton personnage?' Show place cards (maison, école, parc).

mainActivity.activity: Students choose a place for their character and draw simple background. Practice saying where character lives: '[Name] habite [lieu]'.
mainActivity.flexibility: Accept creative places like space, underwater. Support with vocabulary as needed.

closing.activity: Students place character in their setting and share with partner. Simple presentations if time allows.

decisionPoints: If students can't decide on place → Offer choice between 2-3 familiar places
If students choose unusual places → Help them find French words or use gestures
If drawing takes too long → Remind that simple is good, focus on the story
lessons.troubleshooting: If students get frustrated with drawing, use place cards they can choose and point to
lessons.realWorldConnection: Everything happens somewhere - stories need places too, just like where we live and play
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by adding setting to their character

lessons.title: Que fait mon personnage?
lessons.oneGoal: Students plan one simple action for their character
materials: Character and setting from previous lessons

opening.activity: Review: character and place. Now 'Que fait [character name]?' Model actions with gestures.

mainActivity.activity: Students choose one action for their character (courir, manger, jouer). Act out the action, then add it to their character story.
mainActivity.flexibility: Let energetic students act out multiple actions. Quieter students can just point to action cards.

closing.activity: Action circle - students say their character's name and action, class repeats the action together.

decisionPoints: If students choose complex actions → Help simplify to basic verbs
If students are very active → Channel energy into character actions
If students are hesitant → Let them copy actions from classmates
lessons.troubleshooting: If students can't think of actions, start with basic ones they know: walk, eat, sleep
lessons.realWorldConnection: People do things - our characters should too, just like how we do different activities all day
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by adding action to character and setting

lessons.title: Première page d'auteur
lessons.oneGoal: Students create their first story page with picture and one sentence
materials: Character, setting, action from previous lessons

opening.activity: Review all elements: character, setting, action. 'Maintenant, nous créons notre première page d'histoire!'

mainActivity.activity: Students combine their character, setting, and action into one page. Draw picture and write/copy one simple sentence with support.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some may write independently, others may need sentence starters or teacher scribing.

closing.activity: Students admire their first story page. Celebrate: 'Vous êtes des auteurs!' Save pages carefully for tomorrow.

decisionPoints: If writing is too difficult → Let students dictate sentence to teacher or use pictures only
If students want to write more → Encourage but keep focus on one clear sentence
If students struggle with combining elements → Help them focus on just character + action
lessons.troubleshooting: If perfectionism stops progress, remind students that first drafts don't need to be perfect
lessons.realWorldConnection: Every book starts with the first page - just like how we start anything new step by step
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by combining all elements into first page

lessons.title: Partager avec la classe
lessons.oneGoal: Students show their page and read their sentence to a partner

opening.activity: Bring out story pages. 'Hier, nous avons créé nos premières pages. Aujourd'hui, nous partageons avec nos amis.'

mainActivity.activity: Partner sharing - students take turns showing their page and reading/telling their sentence. Switch partners halfway through.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some may read fluently, others may just show pictures and tell in simple words.

closing.activity: Circle sharing - few volunteers share with whole class. Focus on celebration and encouragement.

decisionPoints: If students are shy about sharing → Let them share with teacher first, then partner
If students want to share everything → Set timer for each share to keep it manageable
If reading is difficult → Let students tell their story in their own words
lessons.troubleshooting: If students are too nervous to share, let them just show their picture without words
lessons.realWorldConnection: Authors share their work so others can enjoy it - just like when we show family our artwork
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by sharing their creation with others

lessons.title: Améliorer mon histoire
lessons.oneGoal: Students add one detail to make their story better

opening.activity: Look at story pages together. 'Comment pouvons-nous améliorer nos histoires?' Show examples of adding details.

mainActivity.activity: Students choose one detail to add - color words, feeling words, or size words. Add to picture or sentence with support.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some may add lots of details, others just one color word. Both are perfect.

closing.activity: Compare before and after pages. Celebrate improvements: 'Regardez comme c'est mieux!'

decisionPoints: If students want to change everything → Help them focus on just one small improvement
If students think their story is perfect → Validate but offer one small addition idea
If students are overwhelmed by choices → Offer just two detail options
lessons.troubleshooting: If students are resistant to changes, frame it as 'adding' rather than 'fixing'
lessons.realWorldConnection: We can always make our work a little better - just like when we tidy our room or improve our bike riding
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by learning to revise and improve

lessons.title: Deuxième page magique
lessons.oneGoal: Students create a second page continuing their story

opening.activity: Review first pages. 'Que se passe-t-il après?' Model continuing a story with simple transition.

mainActivity.activity: Students create second page showing what happens next in their story. Support with 'Et puis...' or 'Après...' starters.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some may create complex continuations, others may just show character in new position.

closing.activity: Students put pages together and see their two-page story. Celebrate growth: 'Vous avez écrit une histoire de deux pages!'

decisionPoints: If students can't think what happens next → Suggest simple changes like character moving or feeling different
If students want many pages → Encourage but keep focus on just two pages for now
If students repeat first page → Help them think of one small change or addition
lessons.troubleshooting: If continuing is too hard, let students create a second scene with same character in different activity
lessons.realWorldConnection: Stories continue - there's always more to tell, just like our day has many different parts
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by extending their story to multiple pages

lessons.title: Chaise d'auteur spéciale
lessons.oneGoal: Students sit in the author's chair and read their story to the class

opening.activity: Introduce the special author's chair. 'Cette chaise est pour les vrais auteurs. Vous êtes des auteurs!'

mainActivity.activity: Each student takes turn in author's chair reading their two-page story. Class gives positive comments using simple phrases.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some may read fluently, others may tell story in own words. All are celebrated equally.

closing.activity: Group celebration. Students say what they liked about being authors. Take photo of each student in author's chair.

decisionPoints: If students are nervous → Let them share with just teacher first, or have friend sit nearby
If some students want to skip → Make it optional but encourage gently
If stories are hard to understand → Focus on effort and celebration over comprehension
lessons.troubleshooting: If students freeze up, let them just show their pictures and tell one thing about their story
lessons.realWorldConnection: Authors share their finished work with audiences - just like when musicians perform or artists show paintings
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by celebrating their authorship publicly

lessons.title: Mon livre fini
lessons.oneGoal: Students complete their mini-book and add a cover

opening.activity: Show real books with covers. 'Tous les livres ont une couverture. Nous créons nos couvertures aujourd'hui.'

mainActivity.activity: Students create cover with title and illustration. Staple pages together to make complete book. Practice being proud of their creation.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some may want elaborate covers, others simple ones. Support all choices.

closing.activity: Book parade - students walk around showing completed books. Add books to classroom library with special 'authored by' labels.

decisionPoints: If students struggle with titles → Help them use character name or main action
If students want to keep working → Set gentle time limit but validate their dedication
If students are disappointed with results → Focus on the amazing accomplishment of writing a book
lessons.troubleshooting: If perfectionism delays completion, remind students that published authors also revise after first books
lessons.realWorldConnection: Finished books have covers and titles like real books - now their book can sit with other books on the shelf
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by completing the full book format

lessons.title: Nouvelle aventure créative
lessons.oneGoal: Students explore different story types through play

opening.activity: Review completed books. 'Maintenant, explorons différents types d'histoires!' Show examples: funny, scary, adventure.

mainActivity.activity: Students experiment with different story types through drawing and play. No pressure to complete, just explore creativity.
mainActivity.flexibility: Let students follow their interests - some may prefer funny stories, others adventure or animal stories.

closing.activity: Share discoveries: 'Quel type d'histoire préférez-vous?' Light discussion about different story preferences.

decisionPoints: If students want to stick with original story type → Support their preference while showing other options
If students are overwhelmed by choices → Offer just two story types to choose from
If students create inappropriate content → Redirect gently to classroom-appropriate topics
lessons.troubleshooting: If students can't think of new ideas, let them modify their original character into new situation
lessons.realWorldConnection: There are many different types of stories to create - just like there are different types of games and activities
lessons.progression: Extension - applies learned skills to new creative challenges

lessons.title: Illustrateur professionnel
lessons.oneGoal: Students focus on creating detailed illustrations for stories

opening.activity: Look at detailed illustrations in picture books. 'Certaines personnes sont illustrateurs - ils créent les images pour les livres.'

mainActivity.activity: Students create detailed illustrations focusing on artistic technique. Encourage attention to details, colors, backgrounds.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may be naturally artistic, others need encouragement to try details. All efforts celebrated.

closing.activity: Art gallery walk - students display illustrations and admire each other's artistic work with positive comments.

decisionPoints: If students get frustrated with details → Remind them that practice makes better, not perfect
If students finish quickly → Encourage them to add one more detail or help a friend
If students compare their work negatively → Emphasize unique style and personal expression
lessons.troubleshooting: If students are afraid to 'mess up' good paper, remind them that artists make many drafts
lessons.realWorldConnection: Some people specialize in making pictures for books - their art helps stories come alive
lessons.progression: Extension - deepens illustration skills beyond basic requirements

lessons.title: Histoires ensemble
lessons.oneGoal: Students collaborate to create a group story

opening.activity: Discuss working together: 'Parfois, les auteurs travaillent ensemble.' Model how to share ideas respectfully.

mainActivity.activity: Small groups (3-4 students) create one story together. Each student contributes one element. Practice compromise and sharing ideas.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some groups may work smoothly, others need more teacher support for cooperation.

closing.activity: Groups share their collaborative stories. Celebrate teamwork and different perspectives in one story.

decisionPoints: If groups have conflicts → Teach simple compromise strategies like taking turns
If one student dominates → Gently structure so each student has specific role
If groups finish at different times → Have extension activities ready for early finishers
lessons.troubleshooting: If collaboration is too challenging, let students work in pairs instead of larger groups
lessons.realWorldConnection: Sometimes authors work together to create stories - just like how families work together on projects
lessons.progression: Extension - applies individual skills to collaborative creation

lessons.title: Bibliothèque de classe
lessons.oneGoal: Students organize their books into a class library

opening.activity: Look at all the books students have created. 'Regardez tous ces livres! Nous avons une bibliothèque d'auteurs!'

mainActivity.activity: Students help organize their books into class library. Create categories, make labels, set up checkout system for reading each other's books.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may be very organized, others need support with categorizing. Let interests guide organization.

closing.activity: Admire the completed class library. Students choose one book written by classmate to 'check out' for reading.

decisionPoints: If students have trouble categorizing → Use simple categories like 'funny stories' or 'animal stories'
If students want to keep their own books → Explain that libraries let everyone enjoy books
If organization takes too long → Focus on just getting books displayed nicely
lessons.troubleshooting: If students are protective of their books, start with just displaying them before implementing checkout
lessons.realWorldConnection: Libraries collect books so everyone can read them - now classmates can enjoy each other's stories
lessons.progression: Extension - celebrates collective authorship achievement

lessons.title: Lire aux petits
lessons.oneGoal: Students practice reading their books to younger students

opening.activity: Discuss being 'big kids' who can teach. 'Vous pouvez partager vos histoires avec les petits enfants.'

mainActivity.activity: Students practice reading their books aloud with expression. If possible, visit kindergarten class to share stories, or practice with stuffed animals.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may be natural performers, others need encouragement. Support all comfort levels.

closing.activity: Reflect on being teachers and authors. Discuss how it feels to share stories with others.

decisionPoints: If students are nervous about reading to others → Let them practice with toys or teacher first
If no younger class available → Use stuffed animals or dolls as audience
If students want to read multiple books → Support enthusiasm but manage time
lessons.troubleshooting: If reading aloud is too challenging, let students just show pictures and tell story in simple words
lessons.realWorldConnection: Older students can share stories with younger ones - just like how family members read to each other
lessons.progression: Extension - uses authorship skills to teach others

lessons.title: Célébration d'auteurs
lessons.oneGoal: Students celebrate their growth as young French authors

opening.activity: Look back at journey from Lesson 1 to now. 'Regardez comme vous avez grandi comme auteurs!'

mainActivity.activity: Celebration party with sharing of favorite parts of being authors. Present author certificates. Create memory book of writing journey.
mainActivity.flexibility: Let students share what they're most proud of. Some may focus on writing, others on pictures or sharing.

closing.activity: Final circle: each student completes 'Je suis un auteur parce que...' Group picture with all their books.

decisionPoints: If students want to keep working → Encourage continued writing in free time
If students don't feel like 'real' authors → Emphasize that all writers start somewhere
If celebration feels overwhelming → Keep it simple with just sharing and certificates
lessons.troubleshooting: If some students feel their work isn't good enough, emphasize effort and growth over perfection
lessons.realWorldConnection: Authors celebrate when they finish their work - just like any accomplishment deserves recognition
lessons.progression: Extension - culminates the unit with reflection and celebration
